quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against their red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive past the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them away from crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians always have the right of way. Be careful around pedestrians at all times, even when your light is green.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in an accident?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Stay out of traffic lanes to avoid being hit. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about road conditions ahead.
It helps you find cities and towns.
It tells you about traffic laws.
It tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about road conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background. They alert you to road hazards or conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drivers who drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.
They have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: You hear a fire truck siren behind you. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When a school bus has flashing lights.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, on railroad crossings, or on bridges. Never pass near a school bus with flashing red lights. Only pass when you have a clear view and it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Always make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers are properly restrained. Children age 12 and under should sit in the back seat. Never place rear-facing infant car seats in the front seat with an airbag.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, turn and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is coming.

questions.question: What should you do when backing up your vehicle?

options.text: Turn your head and body to the right and look out the rear window.
Use only your rearview mirror to check for obstacles.
Honk your horn so pedestrians and vehicles know what you are doing.
None of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and body to the right and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, do not rely only on mirrors. Instead, turn your head and body to the right and look out the rear window.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if other cars are coming.
Stop completely. Go when it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection. You do not always have to stop.
Stop only if there is traffic on the other road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must stop completely. Let all cars and people pass first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is hurt.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In a crash, stop and move your car off the road if you can. Call 911 if anyone is hurt. Call police if someone is injured or killed, or if damage is more than $1,000.

questions.question: If you are about to miss your exit on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal, brake, and move quickly to the right.
Continue to the next exit.
Pull to the right and back up carefully to the exit ramp.
Cross the median to exit the other way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not cross traffic to reach your exit. Keep going to the next exit and leave the highway safely.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop right away.
Help anyone who is hurt.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop right away. Move your car out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people, but stop heavy bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency workers.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first goes first.
The driver who arrives last goes first.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave the others to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first goes first.
questions.explanation: All drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The driver who gets there first can go first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: You should not follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate at a railroad crossing:

options.text: If a train is not too close.
If your car will not damage the gate.
If you look both ways first.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at railroad crossings mean you must stop. Do not cross the tracks until the lights stop and gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a gate.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect either driving skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but it harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It affects your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Turn your head quickly to check for other cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check both your side and rearview mirrors for cars behind you. Turn your head to check your blind spot for any cars you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Side road.
Low clearance.
Traffic is merging.
Get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that traffic may enter from a side road ahead.
